content.text: Why a website is essential for local artisans
Today, even artisans need an online presence to stay competitive. A well-designed website can help you attract more local customers and grow your business. Here’s why:
Visibility
: A website lets you be easily found by potential customers searching for your services online.
Credibility
: Having a professional website boosts your credibility and shows you take your craft seriously.
Accessibility
: Your customers can view your services, hours, and contact details anytime—even outside business hours.
Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
To attract more local customers, optimizing your website for search engines is crucial. Here are some tips:
Local Keywords
: Use region-specific keywords like "artisan in Rennes" or "plumber in Rennes".
Meta Tags
: Ensure your title and description tags include relevant, local keywords.
High-quality content
: Publish useful and informative content regularly about your profession, services, and region.
User Experience (UX)
A well-designed website must provide an excellent user experience. Here are some key elements to consider:
Responsive design
: Your site should be accessible and easy to navigate on all devices, including smartphones and tablets.
Intuitive navigation
: Ensure visitors can easily find what they're looking for, whether it's your services, contact details, or opening hours.
Calls to Action (CTA)
: Encourage visitors to contact you or request a quote by placing clear and visible call-to-action buttons.
Social Media Integration
Social media is an excellent way to promote your business and attract more local customers. Here’s how to integrate them into your website:
Share buttons
: Add share buttons on your pages to allow visitors to share your content on their social networks.
Social feeds
: Integrate your social media feeds to showcase your latest posts and encourage visitors to follow you.
Targeted ads
: Use social media ads to target local customers and promote your services.
Customer Testimonials and Reviews
Customer testimonials and reviews are an excellent way to strengthen your credibility and attract more clients. Here’s how to integrate them into your website:
Dedicated Page
: Create a dedicated page for customer testimonials and reviews to showcase positive feedback from your clients.
Service Page Integration
: Add relevant testimonials on the corresponding service pages to build trust with visitors.
Encourage Reviews
: Encourage satisfied customers to leave a review on your website or on platforms like Google My Business.
Conclusion

Optimizing your website to attract more local customers is essential for the success of your craft business. By following these tips, you can improve your visibility, credibility, and accessibility, and thus attract more local clients.

blog/logiciel-gestion-interventions-tech.title: Field Service Management Software: A Tool That Tracks Your Technicians—Even Without Network Coverage
blog/logiciel-gestion-interventions-tech.excerpt: No more lost paperwork on Fridays, photos buried in text messages, or delayed invoices. Discover how a field service management tool transforms operations—even offline.
blog/logiciel-gestion-interventions-tech.metaTitle: Field Service Management Software: Works Offline Too
blog/logiciel-gestion-interventions-tech.metaDescription: Scheduling, on-site signed work orders, photos, and parts—see how a tailored field service management software revolutionizes your technicians’ daily work, even without connectivity.

content.text: Before writing code, I spent five years in a kitchen. So when a walk-in fridge breaks down on a Friday evening, I know what that means: the chef calling three times, the technician arriving between shifts, and the work order scribbled on a corner of the countertop, which will need to be read again on Monday at the office. If we can even read it.

Later, at Kodeva, I worked on a customer service app for field technicians. That’s when I realized something simple: a service call isn’t just an appointment in a schedule. It’s information that needs to get back to the office, complete and quickly. And that’s almost always where it gets stuck.
The real issue isn’t the scheduling—it’s the follow-up.
Most companies that send technicians to their clients know how to schedule. A whiteboard, a shared calendar, an Excel file: by Monday morning, everyone knows where they’re going.

That’s where it gets complicated. The technician finishes the job, fills out a paper form (when they remember), jots down the parts used on the back, takes two photos with their phone, and sends them via SMS to whoever will bother reading them. On Friday, someone at the office re-enters everything. A signature is missing, an arrival time is wrong, a part number is off. The invoice goes out two weeks late—or sometimes it never goes out at all.
No one is doing this wrong. It’s the organization that loses the information along the way.
What a service call management software should actually do
No need for an overcomplicated system. For most maintenance, customer service, or installation SMEs, a good tool comes down to four things:
Scheduling and assignment
: the office assigns the calls, the technician sees them on their phone, with the address, the on-site contact, and the equipment history.
The work order on the phone
: what was done, the time spent, the parts used, the before-and-after photos, and the client’s signature directly on the screen.
Immediate return to the office
: as soon as the work order is validated, it’s back at the office. No re-entry, no forgotten paperwork in the van.
Integration with the rest of the system
: the work order becomes an invoice, the parts are deducted from stock, and the client receives their report by email.

Written like this, it seems obvious. But every company has its own specifics: a mandatory safety checklist, records to note, a maintenance contract to attach. It’s often in these details that generic software becomes cumbersome.
Offline mode: the detail that makes all the difference
If there’s one lesson I’ve learned from this field service app, it’s this:
if the tool doesn’t work in the basement, it won’t be used.

A technician spends much of their day where the network doesn’t reach: boilers, basements, technical rooms, parking lots, dead zones in the countryside. If the app displays an error message at that moment, they pull out their notebook. And two weeks later, everyone’s back to paper.

Offline mode means everything the technician needs is already on their phone when they leave in the morning, they can fill out the work order and get the client’s signature without any connection, and everything syncs automatically as soon as the network returns. For them, nothing changes. For the office, nothing is lost.
It’s one of the first questions I ask when discussing a tool for field teams.
A concrete example: professional kitchen repairs

Take an SME that installs and repairs professional kitchen equipment for restaurants: ovens, walk-in coolers, dishwashers. Six technicians, one office assistant, and a manager who handles quotes in the evenings.

Today, emergencies come in by phone, often during service hours, and the assistant juggles between the schedule and calls. Technicians fill out paper work orders. Every Friday afternoon, she re-enters the week’s data into the billing software. When a restaurant calls back about the same walk-in cooler, no one really knows what was changed last time.

With a tool tailored to them, the day goes differently. The emergency is created in two clicks and sent to the available technician. On-site, they open the equipment file: past interventions, parts already replaced, photos. They note what they’ve done, take photos, and get the manager’s signature on their phone—even deep inside the walk-in cooler where nothing works. As they leave, the report automatically goes to the restaurant, and the invoice is ready in the office that evening.
The manager hasn’t changed jobs. They’ve just stopped wasting time and money between the field and the office.
Off-the-shelf software or custom tool?
Let’s be honest: there are good off-the-shelf field service management software options. If one fits your workflow, take it. It’ll be cheaper and faster, and I’ll say it straight.

Customization makes sense when your work orders have specific needs no tool handles well, when they need to be linked to your inventory or billing system, or when your technicians often work without network access and the off-the-shelf software’s offline mode isn’t reliable. I’ve detailed this choice in a
comparison between SaaS software and custom tools
Budget-wise, most SME tools cost between 5,000 and 15,000 euros upfront, then 100 to 300 euros per month for maintenance. The details are on my
custom business application page
Frequently Asked Questions
My technicians aren’t comfortable with computers, will it work?
That’s exactly who it’s designed for: big buttons, as few fields as possible, photos taken just like in any other app. If filling out the form takes longer than on paper, it’s a failure.
What happens when the phone has no network?
The technician continues as if nothing happened. Everything is saved on the phone and sent to the office as soon as the network returns.
Can we keep our current invoicing software?
Yes. The tool can send validated forms to it, or export them in the format it accepts. No need to change everything at once.
How long for a first version?
A few weeks for a first useful tool: scheduling, work orders, and signatures. The rest comes later, once the team uses it in real life.
Can we talk about this?

If your work orders still get re-entered every Friday, we can start simply: an audit of your current organization and a written action plan, over the phone or via video call. I always begin with the most painful point, give you an honest budget estimate, and if an existing software solution will suffice, I’ll tell you.

content.text: "We're at Klaxo, but we wonder if we're paying too much for what we use." I hear this regularly from driving school managers, and the question deserves a real answer rather than a vague opinion. So, I reviewed Klaxo’s pricing grid on October 11, 2026, as well as those of other driving school software providers that display their prices. Here’s who Klaxo is the right choice for, what makes people hesitate, five alternatives with their pricing, and when a custom tool might cost less.
What Klaxo costs in 2026
Klaxo offers three subscription plans, all with the full set of features, and the price depends on your number of enrollments. As of October 11, 2026, the
Klaxo pricing page

lists the Basic plan at 99 € HT per month for 10 student enrollments, Essentiel at 159 € HT for 25 enrollments, and Premium at 249 € HT for 50 enrollments. Beyond your package, each additional enrollment is billed at 9.90 €. SMS appointment reminders are optional, with no listed price. The page says nothing about contract length, setup fees, or a free trial: you’ll need to request a demo.

An example to set expectations. An agency enrolling 15 students per month pays either 99 € plus 5 enrollments at 9.90 €, totaling 148.50 € HT, or the Essentiel plan at 159 € HT. Over a year, expect to pay between 1,782 € and 1,908 € HT before SMS costs. If your enrollments vary greatly by month, this is the detail to watch: your bill follows your enrollments.
A detail that matters: this pricing page isn’t linked from Klaxo’s homepage. I found it through a link in their article on the cost of driving school software. Couldn’t find it? That’s normal.
Who Klaxo is the right choice for

Klaxo covers every aspect of a driving school’s daily operations in one tool: lesson and exam scheduling, online reservations by students, integrated ANTS enrollment, exam slot reservations, digital logbooks and progress sheets, contracts and digitized files, an online store with three-installment payments, quotes, invoices, and automated reminders. The publisher claims over 6,000 managers, secretaries, and instructors as users, a team of 15, and around 30 new driving schools per month. As of October 11, 2026, its Trustpilot page shows a 4.6 out of 5 rating for 26 reviews.

If you enroll a steady monthly volume of students, want an online store with installment payments, and prefer an established publisher, Klaxo delivers. You pay for the full coverage, and it makes sense.
What makes people hesitate
The starting price.

Among driving school software providers that publish their pricing, Klaxo is the most expensive to start: 99 € HT per month, while others begin between 0 and 79 €. For a small agency with one or two instructors, the difference over three years adds up to thousands of euros.
The per-enrollment price.
The 9.90 € fee per enrollment beyond the package makes the budget unpredictable. A strong September month could cost more than a winter month.
What the page doesn’t say.
No mention of contract length, setup fees, free trial, or SMS pricing. You’ll only find out by requesting a quote. Ask for it in writing, including the data export format if you ever leave.
Five alternatives to Klaxo, with their prices
The prices below are those listed on each publisher’s website, excluding taxes, checked on September 29, 2026 for my
comparison of driving school software
, and verified on October 11th for Drivup.
Drivea
is free, with a 10 € per month option to receive new students. Scheduling, students, payments, progress, iOS and Android apps. To get started with no budget.
Ma Gestion Zen
costs 39 € per month with 3 users included: scheduling, students, fleet, accounting, student portal, ANTS connection, multiple agencies.
Drivup

offers two fixed-price plans per agency: Go at 45 € HT per month and Connect at 69 € HT, with discounts starting from two agencies. The digital workbook is billed from 3.50 € HT per workbook, SMS at 0.094 € HT, and the installation of the payment module by card at 300 € HT. The price does not depend on registrations, but options add up.
Kréno 2

costs 49 € per month up to 200 registrations per year, then 2.70 € per registration. Scheduling, contracts, invoices, certified collections, workbook bound to the State, student and instructor apps. It’s the closest alternative to Klaxo’s model at a lower price per registration.
GestAuto-École
costs 79 € per month, unlimited instructors and students, based on Odoo: scheduling, workbook, student portal, packages, multiple agencies.

For a simple booking calendar, rdv360 has a free plan, then 29.90 to 59.90 € per month with the cash register and online payments. Rapido, Elgéaweb, and AGX, the historical publishers, do not disclose their pricing.
And if none fit: the custom tool

A driving school with its own way of working eventually twists its software. Packages that don’t fit any category, scheduling across multiple agencies with custom rules, tracking hours you still manage on Excel alongside your subscription. I developed a
custom driving school management software
for such situations: scheduling, students and hours, with the client’s rules and nothing else.

On pricing, a custom add-on connected alongside your subscription costs 2,500 to 7,000 € once. A complete software package ranges between 5,000 and 15,000 € upfront with me, then 100 to 300 € per month for maintenance, hosting, and backups included. You own the code and data. Over three years, compare this figure to 36 months of Klaxo Essentiel, which is 5,724 € HT without additional registrations, and you’ll have a real decision-making basis. My
custom software pricing benchmark
provides ranges from 14 French providers to compare.
If your first need is lesson booking by the students, also read my article on the
booking app for driving schools
: what it has to handle, and what it changes at the front desk.
How to Choose in One Day
Start with the
six-question test

on my driving school software page: it tells you whether an off-the-shelf software is enough, if an add-on is necessary, or if customization is justified. Then put the software you're considering through a real day: a registration, a contract, a lesson booked by a student, an invoice, and a driving log extract. Finally, calculate the cost over three years based on your actual registrations—not the introductory price.
Frequently Asked Questions
Does Klaxo offer a free trial?
As of October 11, 2026, its pricing page doesn’t mention it. The site redirects to a demo request. Ask the question in writing, along with the commitment terms.
How much does Klaxo cost for a small driving school?
The cheapest plan is 99 € VAT-exclusive per month for 10 monthly registrations, then 9.90 € per additional registration. SMS are optional.
What’s a free alternative to Klaxo?
Drivea is free, with a 10 €/month option. The free version of rdv360 offers an online calendar with bookings, but no cash register or payment system.
How to switch driving school software without losing data?

Before signing, regardless of the provider, ask for the export format of students, lesson hours, contracts, and invoices. I haven’t verified this for Klaxo. If export is available, migration to another tool takes a few days.
Unsure between subscription and custom software?

Send me a few lines about your workflow: number of branches, monthly registrations, and what’s missing today. I’ll reply within 24 hours with an honest opinion—even if the best answer is to stick with a subscription.

content.text: AutoProGestion often comes up when a mechanic is looking for online management software: it's one of the few publishers in the sector to display its prices upfront. Before recommending anything, I reviewed its pricing grid on October 11, 2026, as well as those of garage software solutions that also publish their rates. Here’s who AutoProGestion is the right choice for, what might make you hesitate, four alternatives with their prices, and when a custom-built tool might be justified.
What AutoProGestion Costs in 2026
As of October 11, 2026, the
AutoProGestion pricing page

lists two plans and a custom quote option. Starter costs 29 € per month for up to 100 clients: unlimited quotes and invoices, online scheduling and appointments, job tracking, repair orders with condition reports, client portal for viewing, maintenance log with QR code, and a limited AI assistant with 10 messages per hour. Pro costs 59 € per month for an unlimited number of clients and adds client portal with remote signature, automatic SMS and email reminders, inventory with alerts, an accounting module with FEC export, used vehicle fleet management (Cerfa forms, police logbook), video inspection, license plate reading, and priority support. The Enterprise plan, multi-site with API, is available upon request.

Both plans are no-contract, cancellable at any time, with a 14-day free trial with no conditions—your card isn’t charged during the trial. Annual payment is advertised at 17% off, though no specific amount is displayed. The page doesn’t specify whether prices are exclusive of tax (HT) or all-inclusive (TTC), and the mobile app for the Pro plan is marked as ‘coming soon.’
Who AutoProGestion Is Right For

An independent garage with one to three employees looking to create quotes, repair orders, and invoices online, book appointments from their website, and give clients access—all at a fixed price with no commitment. If you don’t track inventory and have fewer than 100 active clients, Starter at 29 € per month covers the essentials. If you need automatic reminders, remote signatures, inventory tracking, and accounting exports, go for Pro at 59 €.
What Might Make You Hesitate
The 100-client limit.
A busy garage quickly exceeds 100 client records. In that case, the actual plan you’d need is Pro, at 59 € per month, totaling 708 € per year.
Features split between the two plans.
Inventory tracking, SMS reminders, and remote signatures aren’t included in Starter. Check which plan includes the features you use daily before comparing prices.
What’s Not Yet Available

The mobile app is announced but not yet available as of October 11, 2026, multi-site functionality is available only upon request, and the page doesn’t specify whether prices are HT or TTC. Ask these three questions before committing.
Few Public Reviews
Trustpilot shows a 4.2 out of 5 rating based on 6 reviews as of October 11, 2026. That’s neither a strong positive nor negative signal—it’s too few to draw conclusions. Try the 14-day trial instead.
Four Alternatives to AutoProGestion, With Their Prices
Prices listed on each publisher’s website, checked on September 29, 2026, for my
comparison of garage management software
, and verified on October 11th for Gest'Garage.
Gest'Garage

costs 19 € per month, VAT not applicable, up to 5 employees, no commitment, with 14 days trial without a credit card, and 20% off annually. Everything is included: unlimited quotes, repair orders, and invoices, Factur-X invoices, electronic signature, workshop scheduling and online appointments, parts stock with alerts, and customer SMS. An additional garage under the same SIRET costs 10 € per month. It’s the cheapest alternative, and it already supports Factur-X invoices.
TDV
costs 19.90 to 24.90 € TTC per month. The 19.90 € plan includes only the schedule and time rates; the full 24.90 € plan adds quotes, repair orders, invoices, and parts stock.
Kwixéo
costs 22 to 89 € HT per month, or 18.33 to 74.17 € HT paid annually: vehicles, repair orders, quotes, invoices, and multi-depot stock in the Expert plan.
EBP MéCa and GAD Garage
are available on quote. These are suites with integrated accounting or accounting exports, for garages that want everything from a single provider.
And if none fit: the custom tool

Garage software handles quotes and invoices well. Where they struggle is with what’s unique to your workshop: tracking mechanics’ hours, fleet monitoring for a professional client, or linking quotes, repair orders, added parts mid-process, and invoices without re-entering anything. I developed
Gest-Time
, a time-tracking software, for this exact need: a tool that does one thing, precisely how the business operates. I explain in another article
what a custom tool brings to a garage owner

On pricing, an add-on connected alongside your subscription costs 2,500 to 7,000 € one-time. A full management software ranges from 5,000 to 15,000 € upfront with me, plus 100 to 300 € per month for maintenance, hosting, and backups included, and you own the code. Over three years, AutoProGestion Pro costs 2,124 €. Custom solutions don’t win on this number: they win when your subscription costs you an hour a day in re-entry. My
custom software pricing benchmark
provides price ranges from 14 French providers to verify a quote.
How to Choose in One Day
Do the
test in six questions

from my page on garage software. Then put the software through its paces during its free trial: a quote accepted over the phone, turned into a signed repair order, a part added along the way, the invoice, and the technical inspection reminder six months later. If you enter something once, you’ll have to re-enter it every day.
Frequently Asked Questions
Does AutoProGestion offer a free trial?
Yes, 14 days with no conditions as of its pricing page on October 11, 2026, with no charge during the trial.
What is the cheapest garage software?
Among those that display their prices, Gest'Garage at €19 per month all-inclusive, followed by TDV starting at €19.90 VAT included for the agenda alone.
Does a garage software need to handle electronic invoicing?

From September 1, 2027, SMEs will have to issue invoices in electronic format. Gest'Garage already supports this with Factur-X. For others, ask about the planned implementation date before committing.
What should a garage invoice include?

From €25 VAT inclusive: the date, the garage’s name and address, the customer’s name, the date and location of the service, the details of parts and labor, the subtotals (excluding and including tax), and the mileage. This is the minimum to check on the software you’re testing.
You don’t know which one to choose?
Describe your workshop in a few lines: number of employees, what you still do manually, and what annoys you. I’ll reply within 24 hours, and if a €19 subscription is enough, I’ll let you know.

blog/aides-creation-site-internet-logici.title: Grants for Creating a Website or Software in 2026: What Actually Exists and What No Longer Does
blog/aides-creation-site-internet-logici.excerpt: The France Num check is over, and the Bpifrance loan has ended too. What truly funds a website or software in 2026, the three rules that disqualify you from aid, and where to start.
blog/aides-creation-site-internet-logici.metaTitle: Grants for Website and Software Creation in 2026: What’s Available
blog/aides-creation-site-internet-logici.metaDescription: France Num check discontinued, Bpifrance loan ended. What actually funds a website or software in 2026: local grants, Pass Commerce, tax credits.

content.text: "Isn’t there a €500 grant to create your website?" I still hear that question, and the answer has been no since 2021. When a craftsman or a shopkeeper asks me, I prefer to tell them what actually exists in October 2026 rather than let them search for a dead program on outdated pages. I reviewed the guides from France Num, Bpifrance, the Ministry of Economy, and local authorities to write this guide. Here’s what no longer exists, what still does, and how not to miss out on the help you’re entitled to.
What no longer exists, even though many websites still mention it
The €500 France Num voucher.

Created during the lockdown to help small businesses digitize, it ended in 2021. Well-ranked articles on Google still talk about it in the present tense. If a page promises "the state’s €500 grant to create your website," it’s outdated.
Bpifrance’s Digital Transformation Loan.
This loan of €5,000 to €50,000, co-financed by banks, stopped being offered on December 31, 2023. Bpifrance confirms this on its page.
Free digital diagnostics from the recovery plan.

The Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI) and Chambers of Trades and Crafts (CMA) carried out thousands of these in 2021 and 2022. The national program has ended, though some chambers still offer support on their own initiative.
What exists in 2026 at the national level
There is no national grant for a website or software. What remains changes in nature.
Bpifrance’s Boost Digital Transformation Loan.

This is the successor to the loan that ended in 2023: a no-guarantee loan of €5,000 to €100,000 over three to five years, reserved for companies over three years old that already have an ongoing bank loan and an accountant. Individual businesses are not eligible. This is money to repay, not a grant.
The innovation tax credit.

The 2025 finance law extended it until December 31, 2027, reducing its rate to 20%. It covers 20% of expenses incurred by an SME to design a prototype for a new product, even if the work is outsourced to an approved provider. It does not cover an internal tool, a showcase website, or a management app: it targets a product you plan to sell. If you’re launching software or a platform, ask your accountant before signing, and check if the provider is approved.
The local aid database.

The aides-entreprises.fr website, managed by CMA France and taken over by France Num, lists over 2,000 aids from regions, departments, and local authorities. This is where the real grants for websites or software are found, and they depend on your address.
The real aids that exist are local
In Brittany, the Commerce and Crafts Pass.

This is the most solid program I’ve found for a digital project. The Region and each local authority fund 30% of investments for an independent shop or craftsman, up to €7,500 in aid, with a minimum often set at €6,000 VAT-exclusive per file. Website creation or redesign and online sales modules are almost always accepted; management software may be, depending on the local authority. Rennes Métropole caps aid at €6,000 and only covers towns with fewer than 5,000 inhabitants and priority neighborhoods in Rennes. Bretagne Porte de Loire offers up to 50% funding for digital projects starting at €2,000. I’ve reviewed the 18 regulations of Ille-et-Vilaine and included them in a
grant simulator for your website or software
: your municipality, your project, its amount, and it provides you with the aid, the remaining amount to be paid, and the points to confirm.
Elsewhere in France, regional or intermunicipal schemes exist.

The published guides show very different aids from one territory to another: from a few hundred euros for a basic website in some rural communities to several thousand euros in regions like Grand Est or Hauts-de-France, often as a percentage of expenses with a minimum and maximum threshold. The conditions are summarized in a few lines: company size, turnover, registration, and a request submitted before starting.
For SMEs in production in Brittany, the PASS Transitions.

The Region reimburses 50% of a consulting service of at least €6,000, providing aid of €3,000 to €10,000, for companies with fewer than 50 employees in production or production-related services. Local shops and artisans are not eligible, and the application deadline must be checked.
The three rules that can disqualify you from aid
Applications are rarely rejected for the project itself. They are rejected due to the timeline or the amount.
Submit the request before signing.

In almost all schemes, expenses incurred before submitting the request, or before receiving the acknowledgment of the letter of intent in Brittany, are not eligible. A signed quote from the day before will disqualify you entirely from the aid. Ask first, sign later.
Meeting the minimum threshold.

A basic website costing €1,500 rarely qualifies on its own when the application must reach €6,000 VAT-exclusive. A website with management tools, equipment, or renovations, yes. Bundle your investments into a single application.
Do not include subscriptions.

Hosting, maintenance, monthly software subscriptions, paid advertising, and SEO are never funded. Only development, creation, and training on the tool are eligible. Request a quote that separates these two.
How to proceed, in order

Search for your municipality on aides-entreprises.fr or, in Brittany, use the simulator. Then, call the CCI (Chamber of Commerce and Industry) or CMA (Chamber of Trades and Crafts) in your department: their advisors prepare the applications, know edge cases, and often organize a visit. Submit the request or letter of intent, then only proceed with quotes dated afterward. Allow one to three months for processing, and the aid is paid upon settled invoices, once the project is completed. Plan for cash flow between these steps.

I do not submit the request on your behalf—it’s your file and your signature. But I provide what the chamber expects from a service provider: a quote dated after your letter of intent, detailed line by line, without mixed subscriptions and development, and the technical answers for your advisor. It depends on the region. In Brittany, some intercommunalities mention cash register software or customer relationship tools, while others only cover the website and online sales. Ask for a written response from your advisor before signing.
How much time should I plan for?

One to three months of processing after submitting the complete file, then the project execution, followed by payment on invoices. From the first step to the money in your account, plan often six months.

content.text: There’s a moment every small business manager with inventory knows well. A customer calls for a reference, the file says ‘12 in stock.’ Someone goes to check the warehouse. Only two remain, plus an open box no one knows where it came from.
The file isn’t wrong by chance. It’s wrong because it relies on dozens of small entries that no one has time to input at the right moment.

I worked on this problem during my internship at Kodeva, on StockPME, a stock and inventory management software for SMEs and small businesses, distributed with its hardware by the company Breizhtic. It’s still in use today. Here’s what I learned from it.
Why does a stock spreadsheet always end up being wrong?
A stock spreadsheet works fine as long as only one person manages it, with a single warehouse and few references. Then, discrepancies start to creep in gradually:
- an exit noted on a sticky note, never recorded;
- two people editing the file at the same time, with one version overwriting the other;
- a transfer between two warehouses counted twice, or not at all;
- customer returns placed back on the shelf without anyone re-entering them.

After a few months, no one trusts the file anymore. You recount everything manually before every big order, and the year-end inventory keeps the whole team busy on a Saturday. If that sounds familiar, I’ve listed the
signs it’s time to leave Excel
What a stock management software should do for an SME
The goal isn’t to replicate an ERP from a large corporation. For an SME, the essentials boil down to a few key features:
Clear product sheets
: reference, description, supplier, price, alert threshold, location.
Every movement tracked
: entries, exits, returns, transfers, along with who did it and when. That’s what allows you to understand a discrepancy instead of just suffering through it.
Inventory by location
: if you have a warehouse, a truck, and a store, each has its own inventory, and a transfer happens with a single action.
Threshold alerts
: you know a product is about to run out before promising it to a customer.
A history
: what was used last month, what has been sitting on the shelves for a year.
Nothing spectacular. But when everything is in one place and up to date, inventory becomes reliable information, not just an estimate.
QR code labels: paperless inventory

On StockPME, QR code labels were at the heart of the tool. Each product or location has its own. You scan it with a phone or a reader, and the record opens: you log an outgoing item, a transfer, or a count in seconds, without searching for the reference in a list.

The labels are generated directly from the tool: you select the products, print, and stick them on. When a label gets damaged or a new product arrives, you reprint one in two clicks, without going through a third party.

This is what changes inventory the most. Instead of spending an entire day once a year, you can count one area per week: this is called cycle counting. The inventory stays accurate all year round, and December Saturday becomes a normal one again.
A concrete example: a rental company for event equipment
Take a company that rents equipment for weddings and trade shows: tents, tables, chairs, dishes. Two warehouses, a van, and an inventory that goes out and comes back every weekend.

Today, bookings live in a calendar, inventory in a spreadsheet, and returns are checked by eye on Monday morning. Result: you realize twenty glasses are missing when preparing the next order, and you don’t know if it’s breakage, a counting error, or a box left in the other warehouse.

With the right tool, every outgoing item is scanned when loading, every return when unloading. Breakage is noted immediately, with a photo if needed. Each warehouse’s inventory stays accurate at all times, and before confirming a booking, you see exactly what will be available on the requested date.
The team doesn’t count less. They count at the right time, and only once.
Off-the-shelf software or custom-built tool?

There are many inventory management software options, and some are excellent. If your business is traditional (buy, store, resell), start by looking in that direction: it’s often the right answer, and I explain how to decide in this
comparison between SaaS software and custom solutions

Custom solutions become interesting when your way of working goes beyond the standard: rentals with check-outs and returns, serial numbers or batches to track, multiple warehouses with frequent transfers, or inventory that must communicate with your quoting tool or online store.
For the budget, expect between €5,000 and €15,000 upfront for a small business or SME tool, plus €100 to €300 per month for maintenance. Everything is explained on my
custom business application
page, and you can check out the
StockPME project sheet

Do I need to buy scanners?
Not necessarily. A smartphone often suffices to read a QR code. A dedicated reader becomes useful when scanning a lot—all day long.
Can we import our current Excel file?
Yes. We import it to start with your references and quantities, then perform an initial count to ensure an accurate baseline.
What if multiple people use it at the same time?
That’s exactly the point: everyone records their transactions from their workstation or phone, and everyone sees the same up-to-date inventory.
How long for a first version?
A few weeks for a functional first tool: product sheets, movements, and labels. Alerts, statistics, or integrations with other software come later.

If your inventory lives in a spreadsheet no one really trusts anymore, we can start simply: an audit of your current organization and a written action plan, over the phone or via video call. I always begin with the most critical issue, give you an honest budget estimate, and if an existing software solution works for you, I’ll tell you.

blog/lovable-supabase-base-de-donnees-ou.metaTitle: Lovable and Supabase: Is Your Database Open to Everyone?
blog/lovable-supabase-base-de-donnees-ou.metaDescription: Lovable applications often leave their Supabase tables without access rules. Spend ten minutes checking, and learn what to fix if the database is open.

content.text: "My app Lovable works, but are my data protected?" That’s the first question I ask when someone shows me an AI-generated application, and the answer is often: nobody checked. Lovable, Bolt, and most similar tools store your data in Supabase, a well-built database with one quirk: by default, a table can be readable by anyone who knows your app’s address.

This isn’t a rumor. In May 2025, a vulnerability was published under the name CVE-2025-48757: sites generated by Lovable allowed anyone to read and modify their tables without an account due to insufficient access rules. Lovable responded that data protection remains the responsibility of each client. In other words, it’s up to you to check.
Here’s how to do it in ten minutes, without being a developer, and what to do if the results worry you.
What Row Level Security does, in plain terms

Supabase exposes your database directly to your application through a so-called ‘public’ key that everyone can see in the browser. That’s normal—that’s how the tool works. What prevents strangers from reading your clients’ records isn’t this key: it’s the access rules set on each table, which Supabase calls Row Level Security, or RLS.

For example, a rule might say: ‘A logged-in user only sees rows where the ‘owner’ column holds their ID.’ Without rules, Supabase’s documentation is clear: a table exposed without RLS is readable and modifiable by any role with access, including the public role used by your application.
The issue with AI-generated apps is that these rules are often forgotten or written too broadly to ‘just work’ during a demo. Everything functions, the screens look great, and the door is left open.
Checking in ten minutes
You’ll need access to your Supabase project (Lovable takes you there from the project settings, or you created it yourself).
Open the Supabase dashboard
, then go to the section listing your tables. Each table shows whether RLS is enabled or not. A table marked as unprotected containing names, emails, or orders is the first red flag.
Review the rules for each protected table.
Enabling RLS isn’t enough: you need rules. A rule allowing everyone to read everything, added ‘to make it work,’ is just as bad as having no rules at all.
Test the ‘unknown user’ scenario.
Open your app in a private browsing window without logging in. If other people’s data appears, or if a restricted screen shows up anyway, there’s no protection in place.
Look for keys that shouldn’t be there.

In Supabase settings, there is a so-called service key that bypasses all rules. It must never be found in the application's code. If you see this key in a browser-side configuration file, consider it compromised.
Ten minutes are enough to know if you have a problem. Fixing them takes a little longer.
What I fix when the database is open

On the same day, I lock the door: RLS enabled on every table, and rules that only allow the row owner or the role that needs access to pass through. Then, I verify with two different accounts that one never sees the other’s data, and I write this test to run with every update.

If a service key was lingering in the code, I renew it and move everything using it to the server side. If data could have been read by strangers, I’ll write it to you in black and white, along with what GDPR requires in this case: informing the affected individuals and, when the risk is real, reporting the incident to the CNIL within 72 hours.
This is the first step in
reviving an AI-built application
: securing it, which usually takes three to seven days before addressing any functional bug.
A concrete example

Let’s imagine Karim, who manages a small climbing gym and built with Lovable a member space: sign-up, time slot booking, activity history. Everything works. While running the unknown-user test, he discovers that the member list—with their emails and birthdates—loads even without logging in.

The fix takes one day: access rules per member, a reception role that sees everyone, and an automated test that checks both. The application doesn’t change by a pixel. But the day a member asks, ‘Who can see my data?’, Karim has an answer.
And Bolt, v0, Cursor?

The mechanism is the same: these tools also rely on Supabase or a comparable database, and access rules are just as often missing. The verification above applies to all of them. Only the way to reach the database dashboard changes.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is the public key of Supabase visible in my application a problem?
No, it’s meant to be visible. What matters is that the tables behind have access rules. The key you must never expose is the service key.
Can Lovable fix this on its own if I ask?
It can add rules, but without understanding your business, it often writes them too broadly, and nothing verifies they hold after the next fix. That’s exactly what I review and test.
How much does it cost to secure a Lovable application?
The audit is free. Full security setup (access rules, keys, backups, accounts, and permissions) ranges from 900 to 1,500 € as a flat rate, over three to seven days. Full pricing is on the
AI application recovery page
Should I stop my application to check it?
No. Checking doesn’t affect anything. If the database is open, closing it takes a few hours and happens without disrupting the service.
Should I check yours?

If you don’t want to perform these checks yourself, send me your application’s address. I’ll review the database, rules, and keys, and you’ll receive a written initial assessment within 48 hours, free of charge. You can also start with the
8-question test
, which tells you in two minutes where you stand.

I reviewed its pricing grid on October 11, 2026, as well as those of other driving school software providers that publish their rates. Here’s who Drivup is best suited for, what might make you hesitate, five alternatives with their prices, and when a custom-built tool could actually be cheaper.

Drivup pricing page

lists two offers, excluding taxes, with a per-agency price that decreases based on the number of agencies. Drivup Go costs 45 € per month for one agency, 40 € per agency for two to four agencies, 34 € for five to nine, and 30 € from ten agencies onward. Drivup covers online scheduling with student lesson bookings, a mobile app for students, 24/7 online payments with automated invoicing, electronic signatures, digital logbooks, and integrations with the ANTS system. The Add-Ons You’ll Need to Account For

The logbook, SMS, payment module, and training are all extra on top of the subscription. For a small driving school, these could add up to as much as the subscription itself. Crunch the numbers with your actual volumes.

content.text: "I signed up for the $25 plan, and after ten days, I had no credits left." If you’ve built an app with Lovable, you’ve probably experienced this. The listed price isn’t wrong, but it doesn’t show how much a living, evolving, and growing app truly costs. Here are the numbers as Lovable publishes them, what they actually deliver for a real project, and when a developer becomes cheaper than credits.
The prices below are those displayed in Lovable’s documentation as of October 11, 2026, in dollars. They change regularly: check them before deciding.
What a Lovable subscription costs
Lovable operates on credits. Each subscription provides a set number per month, and each request consumes them.
Free
: 5 build credits per day, capped at 30 per month, plus a few credits for hosting and AI features. Enough to try it out, not to progress.
Pro
: starting at $25 per month for 100 credits ($21 per month if paid annually). The tiers then increase: $50 for 200 credits, $100 for 400, $200 for 800, up to $2,250 per month for 10,000 credits.
Business
: the same tiers, at double the price, with role management, enterprise connection, and priority support.
Top-ups
: $15 for 50 credits on Pro, $30 on Business, valid for twelve months.
One detail that often surprises users: unused monthly credits expire two months after being allocated. What you didn’t use in October is lost by the end of December.
What a request costs

This is where the bill is determined. In build mode, Lovable charges for each message based on the work required. Examples from its own documentation: graying out a button, 0.50 credit; removing the footer, 0.90; adding authentication with signup and login, 1.20; building a homepage with images, 1.70 to 2. In plan mode, each message costs 1 credit.

Two rules heavily impact a buggy project. A request you stop midway is billed for the work already done. And a failed fix costs as much as a successful one. When the AI keeps looping on the same bug, each attempt adds to the total.
What does it look like on a real project?

Let’s take a small management app: clients, quotes, a schedule. The first version is built with 80 to 150 messages, or 100 to 200 credits. With the Pro subscription at 200 credits, $50 per month, it’s doable in one month.

Then comes the phase everyone underestimates: the fixes. A recurring scheduling bug, a failed payment, a screen breaking when fixing another one. It’s not uncommon to spend 40 to 80 credits just on fixes each month. Over six months, including one or two additional tiers and a few top-ups, you easily reach between $400 and $800—not counting your time—for an app that still isn’t stable.
This isn’t a criticism of Lovable: the tool is remarkable for building a prototype in a few days. It’s the model that’s designed for building, not for maintaining an app with users.
The moment when a developer costs less
I see three recurring signals, and when two of them appear, the math changes.
You’re stuck in a loop of paying for fixes.
If, for two months in a row, most of your credits go toward fixing the same issue, you’re paying the subscription without making progress.
There are clients or data involved.
As soon as customer records, payments, or documents pass through the app, the cost of an error far exceeds that of credits. I explain this in the article on
Supabase access rule verification
You no longer dare make any changes.
When every request feels risky, the tool isn’t useful anymore.

In response, my prices are fixed and upfront: the audit is free, a written diagnosis costs €400, securing the app costs €900 to €1,500, and a takeover with deployment costs €2,500 to €6,000. Everything is detailed on the
AI app takeover page
. For an app you use daily, a €3,000 takeover often costs less than a year of tier upgrades and top-ups, and you end up with code you own.
A concrete example

Let’s say Sophie runs a vacation rental agency and built a tool with Lovable to track bookings and cleaning schedules. In spring, the $50 subscription was enough. In summer, fixes piled up: she upgraded to the $100 tier, bought two top-ups, and ended the season having spent nearly $500, with a schedule still showing duplicates.

A free audit would have shown in half an hour that the issue came from how bookings were recorded, not the screens. A targeted takeover, a few days of work, and the duplicates were gone for good. Sophie keeps Lovable for designing new ideas and hands production to a developer.

Can I keep using Lovable while also hiring a developer?
Yes, and it’s often the best setup. The project is synced with a GitHub repository, where the developer works, while you continue designing in the tool. I outline the process in the article on
exporting a Lovable project to GitHub
What happens if I run out of credits?
The build stops, but your published site stays online. However, your app’s AI features and some background services may pause.

Yes: thirty minutes of discussion, a code review and access rules check, and a written first opinion within 48 hours. You then decide—or not—how to proceed.
Do I have to start from scratch if I switch to a developer?
Rarely. In most cases, we keep the interface and user flows, and only rebuild the unstable foundations.

blog/reprendre-application-vibe-coding.title: Reviving a Vibe Coding Application: Save, Strengthen, or Start Over from Scratch?
blog/reprendre-application-vibe-coding.excerpt: Your Lovable-, Bolt-, or Cursor-built app is running ‘almost’ smoothly? How to determine if it can be salvaged—and how a developer can take it over.
blog/reprendre-application-vibe-coding.metaTitle: Reviving a Vibe Coding Application (Lovable, Bolt)
blog/reprendre-application-vibe-coding.metaDescription: An app generated with Lovable, Bolt, or Cursor breaking every time you tweak it? Security, data, payments: how to take it over without losing everything.

content.text: The message often starts the same way: "I built an app with Lovable, it works almost. " The "almost" hides everything else. A page that crashes when two people use it at the same time. A payment that goes through one out of three times. A screen that the AI fixes ten times, only to break something else each time.

I’m not against these tools—quite the opposite. Lovable, Bolt, or Cursor let a manager see their idea take shape over a weekend, without waiting for a quote. It’s a real revolution for testing a project. The problem comes later, the day when clients, employees, or money start flowing through the app.
Here’s how I approach fixing an app built with vibe coding—and how to tell if yours can still be saved.
What exactly is vibe coding?

Vibe coding refers to building an app by describing what you want to an AI, without writing the code yourself. You say, "Add a booking page," the tool generates it, you test it, and you ask again. The most well-known tools usually produce a React app with a Supabase database in the background.
The result looks finished. The screen is clean, the buttons work. But no one has really reviewed what’s underneath—and that’s where the surprises lie.
Signs that an AI-generated app is reaching its limits
After a few weeks, the same issues resurface:
every fix breaks something else
. The AI only sees a snippet of the code at a time, so it fixes one screen and breaks another;
the same code exists in four different versions
, slightly altered, and no one knows which one is actually being used;
it works for you, but not for ten users
. Pages slow down, data gets mixed up when multiple people work at the same time;
you’re too afraid to make any changes
before a client meeting, for fear everything will collapse;
the bill for the tool rises
as you request more corrections.
If you recognize yourself in two or three of these points, it’s not a failure. It’s the moment when a prototype should become a real application.
What I look at first: security and data
Before touching anything, I check what could get expensive.
Who can read what.

On Supabase, the rules preventing a user from seeing another’s data don’t just set themselves. Sometimes, a generated app leaves the database open to anyone who knows the address. That’s the first thing I check, because exposed customer records aren’t just a bug—they’re a legal issue.
Keys left lying around.
A payment or email-sending key written in plaintext in the browser code can be picked up by anyone.
Backups.
I check if there’s a backup of the database and if we know how to restore it. Often, the answer is no.
Payments.

A successful payment is easy. A refund, a deposit, a half-abandoned payment—that’s where generated apps go wrong the most. On Izidoor, the booking platform I worked on for two and a half years, I developed online payments with deposits and refunds: those are the cases that require the most attention.
Carry on, rewrite, or start over?
That’s the real question, and the answer isn’t always the one you hope for.
Carry on and solidify
when the structure holds: we secure it, remove duplicates, add tests on critical parts, and keep building from your code. This is the most common case when the app is recent and not too large.
Rewrite a part
when a specific section is the issue—for example, the entire booking or payment module. We keep the rest.
Starting from a clean slate

when each screen has been pieced together separately and the data is poorly organized. It’s painful to hear, but it’s sometimes cheaper than patching things up for months. Your generated version retains its full value: it’s a living specification. We know exactly what you want, screen by screen, and that cuts the project timeline significantly.

I work with Nuxt, Vue, TypeScript, and Python, and I’ve also worked with React at Kodeva and on Izidoor. So a React application generated by Lovable or Bolt doesn’t scare me, and we don’t have to switch technologies to take it over.
A concrete example

Let’s imagine Claire, who manages three gyms. She built an app in one month with Lovable so her members could book classes. At first, it was perfect. Then school started back: two hundred members at once on Monday mornings, double bookings, a room showing available spots when it was full.

We’d begin with a half-day audit: reviewing the code, database, and access rules, then listing risks from most urgent to least urgent. We’d first fix the double bookings and member data issues before adding any new features. Claire’s app stays online during this process: we work on a copy and switch over when it’s ready.
How much does it cost to take over an application

It depends entirely on what the audit reveals, which is why I always start with one. Strengthening a small app can take just a few days of work. Starting from a clean slate is closer to a standard project: most of the small business and SME tools I build cost between €5,000 and €15,000 as a fixed price, plus €100 to €300 per month for maintenance. Everything is detailed on my
custom business application
And if your needs are standard, I’ll let you know: sometimes, an existing software solution does the job better than a custom-built app, whether generated or not. I explain how to decide in this
comparison between off-the-shelf and custom software
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I have to stop using Lovable or Bolt?
Not necessarily. For testing an idea or designing a new screen, they’re great. The difference is that once the app is live, every change goes through someone reviewing the code.
Do I own the code?
Yes, and it’s a good idea to back it up now on a GitHub repository under your name. That’s also what allows a developer to take it over later.
How long does the audit take?
Usually half a day to a full day for a small app. You’ll receive a written list of risks and fixes, in order of priority.
Can you keep the application online during the update?
Yes. We work on a copy, and your users only see the new version when it’s ready.
Want me to take a look at yours?

If you have an AI-built app that’s starting to worry you, send me the address and a few words about what’s going wrong. We can discuss it over the phone or video call—I’ll review the code, and you’ll leave with a written action plan: what needs fixing immediately, what can wait, and a rough budget estimate. If your app is solid and just needs minor tweaks, I’ll let you know that too.

blog/exporter-projet-lovable-github-fair.title: How to Export Your Lovable Project to GitHub and Hand It Over to a Developer: Step-by-Step Guide
blog/exporter-projet-lovable-github-fair.excerpt: The code is yours, and Lovable is ready for release. Create the repository, grant access without sharing the keys, and collaborate seamlessly without breaking synchronization.
blog/exporter-projet-lovable-github-fair.metaTitle: Exporting a Lovable Project to GitHub for Developers
blog/exporter-projet-lovable-github-fair.metaDescription: Your Lovable code is yours to own. Learn how to create a GitHub repository in your name, grant proper access to a developer, and maintain synchronization effortlessly.

content.text: The question almost always comes up at the same time: "My code is in Lovable, how do I give it to a developer?" The good news is that the code is yours, and Lovable allows you to export it. The less good news is that no one explains the right order of steps or what a developer truly expects from you. Here’s the step-by-step guide, as I explain it to my clients.
What Lovable says about your code

Lovable synchronizes each project with a Git repository hosted on GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket, and the repository is created in your own account. It’s not a static copy: synchronization works both ways. What you modify in Lovable is saved to the repository, and what a developer pushes to the repository comes back into your Lovable project.
Git synchronization is available even with the free plan. Downloading the code as a single archive, however, is only available with paid plans—but you won’t need it if the repository already exists.
Last and most importantly: you own the code and the repository. Disconnecting Lovable deletes nothing—neither from your side nor theirs.
Step 1: Create the GitHub repository under your name
If you don’t already have a GitHub account, create one using your company’s email address—not a freelancer’s or intern’s. This account will be the vault for your application for years to come.
Then, in Lovable:
1. Open the project settings and go to the GitHub section;
2. Connect your GitHub account, then authorize the Lovable app on that account;
3. Link the project: Lovable creates the repository and sends all the code to it.
One rule to never forget: never rename, move, or delete this repository once it’s connected. Synchronization will break, with no way to undo it.
Step 2: Grant the developer access without handing over the keys to the house
A developer doesn’t need your Lovable password or your GitHub password. They need three types of access, which you can revoke at any time:
the GitHub repository
, read-only for auditing, or read-write for maintenance;
the Supabase project
(the database), by inviting them as a member of your organization;
application configuration variables
such as payment keys, email sending, and AI. Pass them through a password manager, never via email.

To make auditing useful, include what isn’t visible in the code: what the application should do, the list of bugs with instructions on how to reproduce them, and the screens most critical to your business. A five-line list is worth more than an hour of video call.
Step 3: let the developer work without breaking synchronization

During the handover, the developer retrieves the code on their machine, fixes it, tests it, and sends it back to the repository. Lovable automatically picks up these changes. Two precautions avoid unpleasant surprises:
do not modify the project in Lovable at the same time
a developer is working on it, or notify them: two people editing the same file simultaneously guarantees a conflict;
server-side functions
(what Lovable calls Edge Functions) modified outside the tool must be redeployed from Lovable or directly from the database.

Once the handover is complete, you have two options. You keep Lovable connected to design new screens, and everything going into production goes through the developer. Or you disconnect the tool, and the application lives from the repository like any other software.
Step 4: verify that you remain the owner
Before considering the matter settled, check these four points:
- the GitHub repository is under an account in your name, and you are its administrator;
- the Supabase project is in an organization you own;
- the domain name and hosting are in your name;
- you know where the keys are, and you can revoke anyone’s access within five minutes.
This is what I deliver at the end of every
application handover done with AI
: a repository in your name, documentation explaining how to launch, back up, and restore the application, and no more dependency on a person or a tool.
A concrete example

Let’s imagine Thomas, who runs a cleaning company and built a scheduling tool for his six employees using Lovable. The tool is useful, but it glitches when it comes to substitutions. Before our first conversation, Thomas connects the project to a GitHub repository created with the company’s address, invites me as a read-only user, and sends me three lines: what the tool does, the substitution bug, and Monday morning’s schedule as the top priority screen.

The audit takes half a day. The bug stems from how absences are recorded, not the screen itself. Ten days later, the fix is in the repository, tested, and Lovable has picked it up. Thomas keeps designing his next ideas in the tool and sends them to me when they’re ready for production.
And Bolt?

Bolt also offers sending the project to GitHub. The principle is the same: a repository in your name, access granted to the developer, and the work is done from the repository. The only difference is the path in the menus.
Frequently Asked Questions
Will I lose my Lovable project if I export it?
No. The project stays in Lovable; the repository is a synchronized copy. You can continue using it.
Can the developer retrieve my code without my consent?
No. Access to the repository is granted and revoked from your GitHub account in a few clicks.
Do I need a paid subscription to export?
Synchronization with GitHub is available from the free plan. Only downloading the code as an archive requires a paid plan.
What if I no longer have access to the account that created the project?

This is the trickiest case: a project created by a former contractor or an intern who has since left. Start by regaining access to the account or ask the owner to transfer the project. Without that, you’ll have to start from the code you can retrieve, and sometimes rebuild parts of it.
Need help with the handover?

If you’ve completed steps 1 and 2, send me the repository link and your three lines. I’ll review the code, and you’ll receive my first written feedback within 48 hours, for free. And if you’re still unsure, the
8-question test
will tell you in two minutes whether your application needs a handover.

blog/logiciel-reservation-en-ligne-sur-m.title: Custom Online Booking Software: What I Learned with Izidoor
blog/logiciel-reservation-en-ligne-sur-m.excerpt: Courses, time slots, equipment, deposits, weather: what an online booking system must truly handle for a leisure facility, backed by real-world experience.
blog/logiciel-reservation-en-ligne-sur-m.metaTitle: Custom Online Booking Software: A Hands-On Experience
blog/logiciel-reservation-en-ligne-sur-m.metaDescription: Sailing schools, surfing, kayaking, leisure centers: what an online booking system needs to manage (availability, deposits, cancellations) and its cost.

content.text: One Saturday in July, at a sailing school. The wind picks up at 9 AM, the afternoon sessions are fully booked, and three families call at the same time to ask if there’s still room tomorrow. Meanwhile, someone is searching through a file to see who paid the deposit and still needs to settle the balance.

I spent two and a half years on days like this, on the other side of the screen. At Izidoor, I worked on a booking and management platform for sailing schools, surf schools, kayak centers, ski resorts, and even museums. When I joined, the product was unstable and had almost no users. When I left, it served around thirty organizations and handled thousands of bookings per season.
What follows is what I learned about what a booking software must truly do—and when customization becomes useful.
A booking software isn’t just a calendar
From the outside, booking an activity seems simple: a date, a time slot, a ‘book’ button. In reality, each organization has its own rules, and that’s where generic software falls short.

A surf session has a set number of spots, but also a minimum skill level, an age requirement, and equipment to prepare for each participant. A sailing course lasts five days, and you don’t book just a Wednesday. A kayak rental is charged by the hour, with boats for one or two people. A museum sells time slots with different pricing for school groups.

This is what’s called the availability engine: the part that decides, in real time, what can still be booked. On Izidoor, it was the core of the product, accounting for multiple criteria at once. If this engine fails, you’ll double-book a spot or, worse, turn away customers when space was still available.
The real features of an online booking platform
Over the seasons, I saw what saves teams time—and what remains a gimmick. Here’s what matters:
booking directly on your own website
, not on a third-party platform where customers no longer see your name. On Izidoor, the booking module integrated with clients’ websites;
online payments with deposits
, and especially refunds when bad weather cancels a session. This is the part that causes the most damage when mismanaged;
an on-site cash register
for those paying at reception, linked to the same bookings to avoid keeping two separate records;
automatic reminders
by email or SMS, which reduce forgetfulness;
a readable schedule for instructors
, who know in the morning whom they are supervising and with what equipment;
simple statistics
: occupancy by activity, weekly revenue figures, to decide on the time slots for the following season.
Conversely, many functions sold as add-ons are never used. It’s better to have a tool that perfectly handles six things than one that handles thirty half-heartedly.
The example of an aquatic center
Let’s take an aquatic center that offers group classes, week-long camps, and paddle rentals.

The customer visits the center’s website, selects ‘children’s camp, week of July 14th,’ enters their child’s age and skill level. The software only offers suitable camps with actual available spots. They pay a deposit online and receive immediate confirmation.

The day before the camp, an SMS reminds them of the time and what to bring. In the morning, the instructor opens their schedule on their phone and sees the list of children, their levels, and the sizes of their wetsuits. If the wind is too strong, reception cancels the session in two clicks, and families are automatically notified and refunded or rescheduled.
At the end of the month, the manager sees which camps fill up in three days and which remain half-empty. They adjust the following year based on data, not just intuition.
Off-the-shelf reservation software or custom-built tool?

There are excellent off-the-shelf reservation software options, and for many activities, that’s the right choice. If you offer simple time slots (a coach, a studio, a room), start by looking into those. I also cover this for
sports coaches
and for
driving schools

Custom solutions become interesting when your rules go beyond the standard: multi-day camps, equipment assignments, pricing that changes by season or participant count, multiple locations, a federation system to exchange data with, or simply the desire to stop paying a commission on every booking. For example, on Izidoor, the platform was connected to the French Sailing Federation and email/SMS services.
Another advantage is that you own the tool. Your customer data stays with you, and you don’t rely on price changes decided elsewhere.
How much does a custom booking software cost?

For a leisure facility or small business, most of the tools I create range between €5,000 and €15,000 as a fixed price, depending on the number of activities, booking rules, and connections to your other software. Maintenance then costs €100 to €300 per month. The exact price is set in the quote before we start. Everything is detailed on my
custom business application
page, and you can see the
Izidoor project brief
Frequently Asked Questions
Can we keep our current website?
Yes. The booking module integrates with your existing site as a standalone block. Customers book without leaving your page.
What happens if the weather cancels a session?
We plan for this from the start: the team cancels with one click, customers are notified, and the software offers a reschedule or triggers a refund based on your rules.
Do instructors need to install an app?
Not necessarily. A phone-accessible schedule via a browser usually suffices in most cases.
Can we start before the season?
It’s actually recommended. A first version with the main activities can be ready in a few weeks, then we refine it based on team feedback.
Let’s talk?

If your bookings still go through phone calls, a spreadsheet, or three disconnected tools, tell me how a busy day goes for you. We can discuss it over the phone or video call, and I’ll provide a written action plan: what to automate first and a rough budget estimate. If an off-the-shelf software already fits your needs, I’ll let you know.

blog/alternative-gad-garage-logiciel-gar.metaDescription: GAD Garage: Windows version 12, limited free version, starting at €85 per quarter. Who it’s for, what holds users back, and three online alternatives with their pricing.

content.text: GAD Garage is one of the oldest garage management software programs installed on PCs in France: it has been around in workshops for over ten years, and several mechanics who write to me still use it. Before writing anything, I reviewed its website on October 20, 2026 (version 12, store, reviews), as well as the pricing grids for online garage software. Here’s why GAD Garage remains the right choice for some, what makes people hesitate in 2026, three alternatives with their prices, and when a custom tool is justified.
What GAD Garage Is in 2026

As of October 20, 2026, GAD Garage’s website presents version 12: a garage management software installed on Windows (Vista, 7, 8, 10, and 11), available as a single workstation or networked with a server. The store lists two products: a free ‘Limited Garage Software’ version and the ‘Garage Software V12 (quarterly)’ starting at 85 €, with no details on what this fee covers, the number of workstations, or whether it is tax-exclusive.

The advertised features include quotes converted into repair orders or invoices, management of vehicle brands, models, and versions, parts and inventory with restocking, single or multi-supplier orders, payment tracking and client/supplier schedules, appointments and workload planning per employee with profitability tracking, SMS sending, web ad publishing, and data import/export. Version 12 adds a breakdown service module, visual tracking of vehicle repair progress, assignment of receivables, and windshield replacement, along with interfaces for industry databases (DAT, GTmotive Estimate, AutoData, FFC, Car-Pass), each requiring a separate subscription from their respective providers.
Who Should Choose GAD Garage

A garage or body shop with fixed PCs, working with experts and insurers (receivables assignment, windshield replacement), quoting using manufacturer databases, and wanting software on their own machines without relying on an internet connection. The reviews posted on the publisher’s website (135 messages as of October 20, 2026, with no numerical ratings and no third-party verification) highlight two points: responsive customer support and a free version that users describe as genuinely free. If you fit this description and your workstations stay in the workshop, GAD Garage has been doing the job for years.
What Makes People Hesitate
Windows only, on-site.

The website does not mention Mac, mobile apps, or browser access. Creating a quote at a customer’s location, checking a schedule from a phone, or managing a second site—all require a workshop PC or server setup.
A price starting at 85 € per quarter, with no pricing grid.

The store lists ‘from,’ without specifying what is included, how many workstations are covered, or whether the amount is tax-exclusive. Request a full quote before comparing it to an online subscription with transparent pricing.
Additional costs for interfaces.

Quoting and technical data databases (DAT, GTmotive, AutoData) require separate subscriptions from their respective publishers. These are invaluable for body shops but unnecessary for a standard mechanics garage.
A ‘limited’ free version, with no list of restrictions.
The website does not specify what is missing. Test it knowing you may need to upgrade the day a feature falls short.
Three Alternatives to GAD Garage, With Their Prices
Prices listed on each publisher’s website, checked on October 20, 2026. All three are cloud-based: no installation required, accessible from the workshop, home, or phone.
Gest'Garage, 19 € per month.

The listed amount is what you pay, with no VAT added, for up to five collaborators, no commitment, a 14-day trial without a credit card, and a 20% discount if paid annually. Everything is included: unlimited quotes, repair orders, and invoices in Factur-X format, electronic signatures, online scheduling and appointments, vehicle records by license plate, stock with alerts, client SMS, used vehicles, and FEC accounting exports. A second garage costs 10 € per month. This is the cheapest alternative.
AutoProGestion, 29 or 59 € tax-exclusive per month.

Starting at €29 VAT-exclusive (€24 VAT-exclusive per year), up to 100 clients and two users: quotes, invoices, scheduling, and online appointments, repair orders with a condition report. Pro at €59 VAT-exclusive (€49 VAT-exclusive per year) removes these limits and adds remote signing, SMS and email reminders, inventory, accounting (FEC, Pennylane connector), and a used vehicle fleet with a logbook. No commitment, 14-day trial. The mobile app is still under development as of October 20, 2026.
Kwixéo, €22 to €89 per month.

Essential, Pro, and Expert plans at €18.33, €49.17, and €74.17 VAT-exclusive per month when paid annually (€22, €59, and €89 per month), with a 14-day trial without a card. Vehicles and repair orders available from the first plan, inventory and payment links in Pro, multi-depot inventory in Expert. It’s a general management software with a garage module: useful if you also sell or rent out vehicles.
To compare these software options in one table and determine which suits your workshop, visit my page
garage software
: a free six-question test, the rules to follow in 2026, and downloadable templates for repair orders and quotes. I’ve also detailed the case of
AutoProGestion
in another article.
And if none of these fit: a custom-built tool

What GAD Garage does well, an online software can do too. Where both fall short is in what’s unique to your workshop: package deals by intervention type with varying rates depending on the vehicle, tracking mechanic hours, fleet monitoring for professional clients, booking appointments, and requesting quotes directly on your own site, tailored to your brand. I developed Gest-Time, a time-tracking software still used by SMEs, for this kind of need: a tool that does one thing, exactly how the business operates.

In terms of pricing, a standalone add-on to your subscription costs between €2,500 and €7,000 once. A complete management software ranges from €5,000 to €15,000 upfront with me, plus €100 to €300 per month for maintenance, hosting, and backups included, and you own the code. Over three years, GAD Garage at €85 per quarter costs at least €1,020, Gest’Garage €684. Custom software doesn’t win on this number: it wins when the software saves you an hour a day by eliminating re-entry or workarounds. My
custom software pricing barometer
provides price ranges from 14 French providers to verify a quote.
How to Choose in One Day

Take the six-question test on my garage software page. Then put the software you’re testing through a real day: a quote accepted over the phone, turned into a signed repair order, a part added midway, the invoice, and a six-month later technical inspection reminder. If you’re re-entering data, you’ll be doing it every day.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is GAD Garage free?
A ‘Limited Garage Software’ version is offered for free on the publisher’s store as of October 20, 2026, without a public list of its limitations. The full version 12 starts at €85 per quarter.
Does GAD Garage work on Mac or mobile?
The publisher’s website only mentions Windows (Vista to 11), for single or networked use. For phone or Mac access, check the online software options mentioned earlier.
How much does GAD Garage cost?

"From 85 €" per quarter for the version 12 according to the store, without details on the items or VAT; interfaces with technical databases are separate subscriptions. Request a written quote with the details.
Which online garage software is the cheapest?
Among those that display their prices, Gest'Garage at 19 € per month all-inclusive, then Kwixéo Essentiel at 22 € and AutoProGestion Starter at 29 € VAT-exclusive.
Can you retrieve your data from GAD Garage?

The software claims to support data import and export. Export customers, vehicles, and invoices before switching, and ensure the new tool can import them; in a custom tool, data migration is part of the quote.
You don’t know which one to choose?
