content.text: Gest'Garage is the cheapest garage software among those that display their prices: 19 € per month, all-inclusive. It’s also the one I mention first to a lone mechanic asking where to start. Before recommending anything, I re-read their page on October 20, 2026, then compared the pricing grids of other garage software providers that publish their rates. Here’s who Gest'Garage is best suited for, what might make you hesitate, three alternatives with their prices, and when a custom tool might be justified.
What Gest'Garage Costs in 2026

As of October 20, 2026, Gest'Garage offers a single plan at 19 € per month. This is the amount you pay—the publisher is VAT-exempt, so no VAT is added. No contract is required; cancellation is online, with a 14-day free trial (no credit card needed), and a 20% discount for annual payment (though the discounted price isn’t displayed). Up to five collaborators are included; beyond that, you must contact the publisher. An additional garage under the same account costs 10 € per month or 96 € per year.

Everything is included in the plan: unlimited quotes, repair orders, and invoices; invoices in Factur-X format and receipt via an approved platform; electronic signatures for quotes and repair orders; advance invoices and credits; FEC accounting export; URSSAF declaration assistance for sole traders; a quote request form for your website; workshop scheduling and online appointment booking; customer and vehicle records entered via license plate; parts inventory with alerts; used vehicle sales with detailed records and ads; included SMS (appointment reminders, vehicle ready notifications, follow-ups); email campaigns up to 5,000 sends per month; setup and one hour of training; client file migration; hosting in France; ten-year archiving; and data export at any time.
Who Gest'Garage Is Best For

An independent garage with one to five employees, operating from a single location, wanting to create quotes, repair orders, and invoices online, book appointments via their website, and send SMS—all for a fixed, easy-to-understand price. If you’re still invoicing on Excel or a notebook and your needs match those of a standard mechanics workshop, this is the first software to try: the 14-day trial doesn’t require a credit card, and client file migration is included.
What Might Make You Hesitate
An independent publisher.

Gest'Garage is developed by a single person, VAT-exempt. This keeps costs low but raises questions about continuity: who will respond if the publisher stops? The reassuring points are the ability to export your data at any time and the ten-year archiving mentioned on their page. Perform an export in the first month to verify it’s complete.
No manufacturer pricing databases.

The page doesn’t mention timed estimates, parts catalogs, or integration with technical databases (DAT, GTmotive, AutoData). A body shop that relies on expert pricing or a garage that uses manufacturer times will find this lacking.
Five collaborators, one site.
Beyond five users, pricing isn’t public; each additional garage adds 10 € per month. A network of multiple workshops should compare this with multi-site plans from other publishers.
No mobile app announced.
The page doesn’t mention iOS or Android apps—the software is browser-based, including on mobile. Test entering a repair order from your phone during the trial.
Three Alternatives to Gest'Garage, With Their Prices
Prices listed on each publisher’s website, checked on October 20, 2026.
AutoProGestion, 29 or 59 € HT per month.

Starter at 29 € HT (24 € HT annually), up to 100 clients and two users: quotes, invoices, scheduling, and online appointments; repair orders with condition reports; maintenance logs with QR codes; cash register. Pro at 59 € HT (49 € HT annually): unlimited clients and users; remote signatures; SMS and email reminders; inventory; FEC accounting and Pennylane connector; used vehicle fleet with police records; vehicle video inspections; license plate and registration reading. An Enterprise plan (custom quote) for multiple locations. No contract; 14-day trial; mobile app in development.
Kwixéo, 22 to 89 € per month.

Essential, Pro, and Expert plans at €18.33, €49.17, and €74.17 VAT-exclusive per month when paid annually (€22, €59, and €89 per month), with a 14-day free trial without a card. Vehicles and repair orders from Essential, inventory and payment links from Pro, multi-depot inventory from Expert. A general management software with a garage module: the right choice if you also sell parts or accessories, or if you rent out vehicles.
GAD Garage, starting at €85 per quarter.

The software runs on Windows, version 12, with a limited free version and technical database integrations (DAT, GTmotive, AutoData) available as separate subscriptions. For a workshop that wants its data on its own machines and works with experts. I’ve covered
GAD Garage
in another article.
To compare these software options in one table and determine which suits your workshop, visit my page on
automotive garage software
: a free six-question test, the 2026 compliance rules, and downloadable repair order and estimate templates. The case of
AutoProGestion
also has its own article.
If none of these fit: the custom solution

Gest'Garage handles estimates, repair orders, and invoices for a standard auto mechanics garage very well. Where it falls short—like other market software—is in features specific to your workshop: flat-rate pricing by service type with varying rates per vehicle, tracking mechanic hours, fleet management for professional clients, and multiple workshops with separate inventory and schedules. I developed Gest-Time, a mechanic hour-tracking software still used by SMEs, for this kind of need: a tool that does one thing, exactly as the business operates.

Pricing-wise, a custom add-on next to your subscription costs €2,500 to €7,000 once. A full management software ranges from €5,000 to €15,000 upfront with me, plus €100 to €300 per month for maintenance, hosting, and backups included, and you own the code. Over three years, Gest'Garage costs €684. Custom solutions never beat this number: they win when a subscription costs you an hour daily in re-entry or workarounds. My

How to Choose in One Day

Take the six-question test on my garage software page. Then run the software through a full day during its free trial: a phone-approved estimate turned into a signed repair order, a part added mid-process, the invoice, and a six-month technical inspection reminder. If you re-enter data once, you’ll do it every day.

Yes, 14 days without a credit card until October 20, 2026, with all features, then €19 per month with no commitment.

The displayed amount, 19 € per month, is what you pay: the publisher is VAT-exempt (Article 293 B of the French Tax Code), so no VAT needs to be added. For you, it’s a VAT-free expense that you can reclaim.

The page mentions invoices in Factur-X format and receipt via an approved platform. SMEs will have to issue electronic invoices starting September 1, 2027; this is already addressed with this publisher, but check with others.
What alternative to Gest'Garage is there for multiple workshops?

AutoProGestion offers an Enterprise package on quote with a group view; with Gest'Garage, each additional garage costs 10 € per month under the same account. Beyond two or three locations, a custom solution with scheduling and stock per site becomes an option.
Can you leave Gest'Garage without losing your history?

blog/faille-php-octobre-2026-site-boutiq.title: October 2026 PHP Vulnerabilities: Is Your Website, Store, or Software Affected, and What Should You Do?
blog/faille-php-octobre-2026-site-boutiq.excerpt: Two critical vulnerabilities in PHP were patched on October 21, 2026. Are your WordPress sites, PrestaShop or WooCommerce stores, custom business software, or internal networks at risk? Learn who is impacted, what your hosting provider is doing, and what actions you should take today.
blog/faille-php-octobre-2026-site-boutiq.metaTitle: October 2026 PHP Vulnerabilities: Is Your Website at Risk?
blog/faille-php-octobre-2026-site-boutiq.metaDescription: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities were patched on October 21, 2026. Learn which WordPress sites, PrestaShop stores, and business applications are affected—and what steps you should take now.

content.text: On October 21, 2026, just before 4 PM, the PHP team released four patched versions to fix two critical vulnerabilities that allow taking control of a server without a password. PHP is the language powering WordPress, PrestaShop, WooCommerce, Joomla, Drupal, Magento, and a significant portion of custom business software, intranets, and customer portals built by agencies or freelancers. In other words: if you have a website, an online store, or a management tool accessible over the internet, there’s a good chance it’s affected.
If you only read one paragraph:

the fix is applied on the server, not in WordPress or a plugin. In shared hosting (OVHcloud, o2switch, IONOS, Hostinger, Infomaniak, PlanetHoster…), it’s the hosting provider that installs the new PHP version, but it’s up to you to check if they’ve done it and to switch versions yourself if your site is still running PHP 8.1 or an older version. To check your status in ten seconds, I’ve put online a
free tool that reads your homepage and tells you if your site is affected
What happened on October 21

The two vulnerabilities are referenced as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with the nickname PHP2Shell. They are rated 9.2 out of 10. In practice, a well-crafted web request is enough to execute code on the server, even before the website or application starts. No account, no password, and no need for the site to have a bug: the flaw is in PHP itself.

The story began with a leak. On Monday, October 20, a post on Hacker News announced two critical vulnerabilities under embargo. The company watchTowr confirmed that evening that they were real, and PHP announced a patch for the following day at 2 PM UTC. In the meantime, pages claiming to publish an exploit circulated, Cloudflare activated firewall rules for all its clients as early as 3:02 AM UTC, and saw attackers modifying their payloads to bypass them. The patches were released on Wednesday with a slight lead: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
The most telling signal:

in the afternoon, the French Ministry of the Interior took all prefecture websites offline at the request of ANSSI, citing « preventive maintenance of all its internet sites exposed to a critical security vulnerability, » and Météo-France closed its forecast and alert sites on its own initiative. Part of the tax authority’s portal was also taken down, according to the press. The Netherlands shut down DigiD and MijnOverheid, Finland its online public services, British local councils and Danish services did the same. None of these sites reported any breaches: it was a precautionary measure, exactly what CERT-FR recommends when you can’t patch immediately. If the government shuts down its own sites rather than take the risk, a business website running PHP has no reason to think it’s safe.
The game-changing detail:

PHP 8.1, 8.0, 7.4, and older versions will no longer receive updates. The project released source patches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, which users must compile themselves or obtain from their host, but no official version will be automatically installed. According to W3Techs, about one in four PHP sites still runs on PHP 7. If that’s yours, no one will fix it for you.

CERT-FR, the ANSSI team, issued the same-day alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-014: isolate affected systems, then switch to a maintained and patched version. Workarounds circulating, like disabling session.upload_progress or blocking file uploads, reduce the attack surface for one of the two flaws. They do not replace the update.
What is PHP2Shell?

The nickname given to the two vulnerabilities: a specially crafted web request allows executing commands on the server—a « shell »—through PHP, without an account or password. There is no PHP2Shell virus to hunt for on your computer. It’s a flaw in the PHP engine itself, on the server, and it’s fixed by the October 21 versions.
Which PHP versions are patched?
The fix only exists for still-supported branches.
PHP 8.5
is updated to 8.5.12,
PHP 8.4
PHP 8.3
in 8.3.36 and
PHP 8.2
in 8.2.35, and it’s the last corrected branch: it ends on December 31, 2026, so switching to 8.3 or 8.4 is unavoidable before the end of the year.
PHP 8.1
has been end-of-life since December 31, 2025,
PHP 8.0 and 7.4
for much longer: for these three, PHP has released source patches to compile yourself, and some hosts or Linux distributions include them in their packages.
PHP 7.3 and older, PHP 5
: nothing, and watchTowr considers all versions since PHP 5.4 affected. Switching branches is the only solution.
The number that matters is the one your site actually uses, not the one from a server command line: hosting can run multiple versions side by side.
How to check your PHP version at OVH, o2switch, IONOS, or Infomaniak
On WordPress or WooCommerce:
Tools, then Site Health, tab Info, section Server, line « PHP Version ». Updating WordPress, a theme, or a plugin does not change this number.
At o2switch:
in cPanel, under Software, the tool « Select a PHP Version » displays the current version in a dropdown menu. Choose 8.3 or 8.4, then « Apply », leaving default extensions checked.
At OVHcloud:

customer space, Web Cloud, Hosting, your hosting, tab General Information, line « Global PHP Version ». To change it, in the Configuration section, click the « … » button, then « Modify Configuration ». Those comfortable with it can also edit the line app.engine.version in the .ovhconfig file at the root of the FTP.
At IONOS:
Customer area, Hosting section, PHP menu, click « Open », check the domain, « Modify PHP version », select and save. The switch takes a few minutes.
At Infomaniak:
Manager, Web Hosting, click on the product name, « More information », « Modify », choose the version, « Save ». The change is immediate, and reverting to a vulnerable version is then blocked.
On a VPS, a dedicated server, or Plesk:

In Plesk, Websites & Domains, PHP section for each site. On a server, `php -v` shows the version in the command line, but it’s the `phpinfo()` page or the X-Powered-By header that reveals which version actually serves the site. Then use `apt` or `dnf` to update, followed by a restart of PHP-FPM or Apache.
In all cases, the versions to check for are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12.
The verification tool
reads the version number when the server displays it and recognizes the host to guide you through the correct steps.
Are you affected? Website, store, software, intranet
We often talk about « websites », but the vulnerability doesn’t depend on what you call it. It depends on what’s running on the server.
Your showcase website
running on WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, SPIP, or TYPO3 uses PHP. Affected.
Your online store
running on PrestaShop, WooCommerce, Magento, or Thelia uses PHP. Affected—and it’s the most appealing target for an attacker: there are payments and addresses involved.
Your custom software, intranet, extranet, or customer portal

, if they were developed in PHP (Laravel, Symfony, or custom code), are affected even if they’re password-protected. The vulnerability occurs before the login page. An internal tool used only by your employees but accessible over the internet is exposed like a public site.
Tools installed on a server
, such as Dolibarr, GLPI, Nextcloud, Moodle, a phpBB forum, a wiki, or a ticketing tool, are in the same situation.
Not affected:

website builders like Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, Webflow, Jimdo, or Google Sites. They don’t run PHP for you, and they manage their own servers. An application built in Node.js, Python, or .NET isn’t affected by this vulnerability either. Small caveat: Node.js released its own security patches the same day, October 21. Same reflex, same timing.
If you don’t know what your site runs on,
the verification tool

will tell you on your homepage: it detects the platform, the PHP version when displayed, and often the hosting provider. Otherwise, the question to ask your service provider boils down to this: « which PHP version is this site using, and has it been updated since October 21st? »
What your hosting provider does, and what they don’t do

In shared hosting, PHP belongs to the provider. You can’t install it yourself; you only choose a branch (8.1, 8.2, 8.3…) in your account. The provider, however, installs patched versions on their servers for branches still supported, from 8.2 to 8.5.

As of October 21st in the evening, here’s what I could find. o2switch disabled the affected functionality as early as 8:07 AM, but at 4:40 PM, their servers were still running versions from October 6th, waiting for CloudLinux packages scheduled for that evening. OVHcloud announced firewall rules on their shared clusters and a maintenance campaign. Infomaniak opened a maintenance window from 3:00 PM to 3:00 AM the next day, with fixes deployed by their teams and no action required, except for sites still running an older PHP version. For IONOS, Hostinger, PlanetHoster, LWS, or Gandi, I found no public announcement at that time.
What you need to do in any case:

check in a day or two whether the version has actually changed. An announced patch isn’t necessarily an installed patch. And if your site is on PHP 8.1 or earlier, your host won’t touch it: it’s up to you to upgrade to 8.3 or 8.4 via cPanel, Plesk, or your client portal, after backing up and testing, because an old theme or plugin might not be compatible.
The three questions to ask your service provider
Many sites and tools were built three, five, or eight years ago by an agency or freelancer you no longer see. Now is the time to reach out to them via email to keep a record.
First question:
what PHP version is the site or application currently using? The answer should be a specific number, like 8.3.36, not ‘it’s up to date.’
Second question:
has it been updated since October 21st, 2026, and by whom?
Third question:
have server logs been reviewed since October 20th? Large multipart POST requests targeting pages that don’t normally receive them are the red flag to look for.
If no one responds within the day, or if the provider no longer exists, that’s exactly the kind of situation I handle: I take over access, update, test, and let you know what was done.
And if your site is still running on PHP 7 or 8.1?
This is the trickiest and most common scenario among small businesses. Two options.
The backported package:

Some hosting providers and certain Linux distributions (Debian, Ubuntu) integrate patches into their older versions without changing the version number. You should ask them, in writing, if they have done so. An old version number does not prove the vulnerability on its own, but in case of doubt, confirmation is needed.
Switching branches:

moving to PHP 8.3 or 8.4. That’s the real solution, and it’s also what you’ll have to do anyway, since PHP 8.2 ends on December 31, 2026. It requires checking that your CMS, theme, and extensions support the new version, making a backup outside the server, and testing on a copy before switching. One hour for a simple site, half a day for a store with many modules.
If neither of these options is possible today, the CERT-FR’s recommendation is clear: take the application offline, or place it behind an application firewall, until the necessary steps are taken.
Tax authorities, prefectures, Météo-France: when will they be back, and should we worry?

If you landed here because impots.gouv.fr displays ‘under maintenance’ or your prefecture’s website isn’t responding: it’s this vulnerability, and it’s intentional. The Ministry of the Interior speaks of ‘preventive maintenance’ and ‘better timelines’ for bringing them back online, while Météo-France states that the update is published but that its checks must be completed before reopening. No date was announced by the evening of October 21st, so expect hours rather than weeks. Your data is not at risk, no breach has been announced, and there’s nothing you need to do for these sites.

One precaution: emails and SMS claiming to come from the tax authorities, your hosting provider, or ‘ANSSI’ to ‘verify your credentials’ will flood in over the coming days. Scams always follow this kind of news.
Updating WordPress isn’t enough

This is the most common confusion I hear. ‘I’ve done the updates, everything’s green.’ WordPress, PrestaShop, or plugin updates don’t affect PHP, which runs underneath. A security plugin may block some requests, but not all, and attackers have already modified their payloads to bypass Cloudflare rules. The only real fix is updating PHP on the server.
How to know if it’s already too late
The first attack attempts were observed in the morning of October 21st, even before the patch was released. If your site remained exposed all day, you need to check.

In your server’s access logs, look for unusual multipart POST requests since October 20th. In your file upload directories (uploads, cache, tmp), check for recent .php files you didn’t place there. In your admin panel, look for unknown administrator accounts and new scheduled tasks. If in doubt: immediate backup, change all admin passwords, and if customer personal data is involved, notify the CNIL within 72 hours.
What I can do for you

I’m a freelance developer near Rennes and work remotely across France. For this vulnerability, I do something simple: I check the actual PHP version running on your site, store, or tool, update PHP or switch branches, verify everything still works, and write you a report of what was done. If your provider isn’t responding, I can recover access and take over.
Start by
checking your site for free
, it takes ten seconds. And if the result isn’t what you expected,
write to me
: I’ll respond within 24 hours.
